cards.text: Jacob is still on the road to find his uncle Laban, his mother's brother (Genesis 28:2). He reaches the land of the people of the east and spots a well in a field, with three flocks of sheep lying near it. A large stone covers the mouth of that well.

cards.question: A big stone sits over the well in that field. When do the shepherds roll it away to water the sheep?

answers.text: Once all the flocks are gathered there
Once each shepherd pays the owner

cards.text: Jacob walks up to the shepherds by the well. "My brothers," Jacob asks the shepherds, "where are you from?"

cards.question: Jacob is out looking for his uncle Laban. Where do these shepherds at the well say they're from?

cards.text: HARAN is the very town Jacob set out for (Genesis 28:10), so that's like grabbing the one cookie cutter you wanted from a dark cupboard on the FIRST try. Jacob asks them, "Do you know Laban the grandson of Nahor?"

cards.question: Jacob asks the shepherds if they know Laban the grandson of Nahor. True or false: the shepherds have never heard of Laban.
Jacob asks if Laban is well. The shepherds say yes, and then they point out Laban's daughter coming with his sheep. What's her name?

cards.text: Jacob points out to the shepherds that it's still broad daylight and not yet time to gather the livestock.

cards.question: Since it's still broad daylight, Jacob tells the shepherds to water the sheep and take them back to ___.

cards.text: He JUST met these guys, and he's already running the well. The shepherds tell him they can't, not until all the flocks are gathered and the stone is rolled away.
While Jacob is still talking, Rachel arrives with her father's sheep, because she's a shepherdess.

cards.question: The shepherds won't move the stone off the well until every flock shows up. True or false: as soon as Jacob sees Rachel with Laban's sheep, he rolls the stone away himself.

cards.text: Jacob waters his uncle's sheep. Then Jacob kisses Rachel and weeps aloud.

cards.question: Jacob tells Rachel he is Rebekah's son, a relative of her father. What does Rachel do?

answers.text: Asks him to wait by the well
Sends a shepherd to fetch Laban

cards.question: Rachel runs and tells her father that his sister's son Jacob is here. True or false: Laban waits at home for Jacob to come to him.

cards.text: Laban runs out to meet Jacob, embraces him, kisses him and brings him home. Jacob tells him all that had happened.
Jacob is in his uncle Laban's home now, and Laban has something to say about him.

cards.question: After Jacob tells Laban all that had happened, Laban speaks up. True or false: Laban says Jacob is indeed his own flesh and blood.

cards.text: Jacob stays with Laban a whole month. After my years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, a month with family sounds like a VACATION.
Then Laban says to him, "Just because you are my relative, should you work for nothing?"

cards.question: Laban doesn't want his relative working for nothing. So Laban asks Jacob to tell him what his ___ should be.

cards.text: Now, Laban has two daughters, Leah and Rachel. Remember those names, friend, because you're gonna NEED them.

cards.question: Laban has two daughters, Leah and Rachel. True or false: Rachel is the older one.

cards.text: Leah has weak eyes, but Rachel is shapely and beautiful. And Jacob loves Rachel.

cards.question: Laban wants Jacob to name his price, and Jacob loves Rachel. So Jacob offers ___ years of work for Laban's younger daughter Rachel.
Jacob offers seven years of work for Rachel. What does Laban say about giving her to Jacob?

answers.text: It's better than giving her to another
Jacob must ask his father Isaac first
Rachel has to agree to it first

cards.question: Laban agrees: "Stay here with me." So Jacob serves seven years for Rachel. How do those seven years feel to Jacob?

cards.text: SEVEN YEARS, and to Jacob it feels like a few days, because of his love for her. Friend, I can't wait seven MINUTES for a batch to cool without sneaking one.
The seven years are up, and Jacob tells Laban, "Grant me my wife, for my time is complete…" So Laban invites all the men of that place and prepares a feast.

cards.question: Laban has thrown a feast for the wedding. True or false: when evening comes, Laban gives his daughter Rachel to Jacob.

cards.text: Laban gives Jacob his daughter Leah. He also gives his servant girl Zilpah to Leah as her maidservant.
Then morning comes, and… "there was Leah!"

cards.question: Jacob goes straight to Laban: "Wasn't it for Rachel that I served you?" According to Jacob, what has Laban done to him?
Laban answers Jacob with a custom. What does Laban say isn't done in their land?

answers.text: Marrying off the younger daughter before the older
Holding a wedding feast for a relative from far away
Letting a groom work off the price of his bride

cards.text: NOW we hear about this custom, seven years and a wedding feast later? That's fine print showing up AFTER you sign, friend.

cards.question: Laban tells Jacob to finish this week's celebration, and then Rachel can be his wife too. What does Laban want in return?
Laban offers Rachel for another seven years of work. True or false: Jacob turns the deal down and heads back home.

cards.text: Jacob finishes the week's celebration, and Laban gives him Rachel as his wife. Laban also gives his servant girl Bilhah to Rachel as her maidservant.

cards.question: Jacob is married to both of Laban's daughters now. True or false: Jacob loves Rachel more than Leah.

cards.text: So Jacob works for Laban another seven years. Hang on, friend, because this family's story is FAR from over.
